newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Price rise seen revenue-positive for Lion.
newsitem.headline: Price rise seen revenue-positive for Lion.

text.p: A price rise announced by brewer Lion Nathan late on Thursday was expected to be "revenue-positive" for the company, spokesman Peter Hallwright said.

In a statement Lion Nathan Breweries said it was raising its New Zealand prices by an average of 1.6 percent from June 1 -- the date from which the New Zealand government excise on beer rises by 2.0 percent.
While declining to specify the changes, Hallwright told the New Zealand Press Association the company had a policy of recovering all rises in excise and inflation when it adjusted its prices.
It was also taking the opportunity to adjust some of the relativities between packaging types, brands and regions.
Hallwright said the company had no way of knowing what the impact of the rises would be on it until the retailers adjusted their prices and customers reacted to them.
"We expect it to be revenue-positive but we don't know by how much," he said.
